newsitem.title: USA: Spot soyoil supplies at U.S. Gulf said to be tight.
newsitem.headline: Spot soyoil supplies at U.S. Gulf said to be tight.

text.p: Supplies of soybean oil at the U.S. Gulf were said to be tight as dealers scrambled to find enough soyoil to load a vessel set for sail on Dec 12, according to U.S. exporters.
"Things are pretty tight down there right now," one cash source said. "I'm not sure the tightness will last, but they're having trouble loading right now."

Recent business to China caused the amount of soyoil available for nearby shipment from the Gulf to shrink, sources said. U.S. exporters estimated that 45,000 tonnes of soyoil destined for China has been loaded at the Gulf since Friday "I don't think there's any volume for December right now," said one exporter. "There's a lot of business that's been done."

According to the latest export sales data from the U.S. Department of Agriculture, 15,400 tonnes of soyoil was sold during the week ended Nov. 28, with 13,300 of those sales going to unknown destinations.

Traders said the recent export business helped CBOT soyoil stave off spillover losses from the soybean pit. As of 1220 CST, January soyoil was up 0.02 cent per pound at 22.93, while January soybeans were down 6-1/2 cent at 6.90-1/2 per bushel.
